label: Person
name: Abraham of Freising
summary:
Abraham of Freising (957–994) was Bishop of Freising in Bavaria, one of the most important episcopal sees in the early medieval German Church. He served as bishop under Emperor Otto II and Otto III, participating in the Ottonian imperial Church that was building the institutional framework of the Holy Roman Empire's ecclesiastical structure. His episcopate is documented in the rich archive of the Diocese of Freising, one of the best-preserved medieval German episcopal archives.

Freising was a seat of exceptional importance in the Bavarian Church: it had been founded in the early eighth century by Saint Corbinian and had the most important episcopal scriptorium in Bavaria, producing manuscript illumination of high quality. The Freising Fragments — the oldest known texts written in a Slavic language, dating from around Abraham's time — were produced in a Freising context, suggesting the diocese's engagement with Slavic missions east of Bavaria.

Abraham's episcopate contributed to the continuing development of Freising's ecclesiastical infrastructure — its cathedral chapter, its scriptorium, and its role in the Ottonian imperial Church's integration of Bavaria into the larger German ecclesiastical network. His participation in Ottonian church councils and his administration of one of Bavaria's most prestigious sees made him a significant figure in tenth-century German ecclesiastical life.
